# NOTES ON TWO BOOKS

## BOOK 1 of 2: "The Case of the Black Twenty-Two" by Brian Flynn (1929)

**Chapter list:** I Mr. Daventry Receives a Commission; II Schedule Numbers 37, 38 and 39; III The Hanover Galleries Murder; IV Peter Daventry Is Mindful of Mr. Bathurst; V The Assynton Lodge Murder; VI Marjorie Lennox Doesn't Mince Matters; VII Butterworth Is Apprehensive of the Future; VIII The 6:55 Carries a Trio of Distinction; IX Mr. Bathurst Opens His Bedroom Door; X The Incident of the Boot-Boy's Bicycle; XI With a Given Center, Mr. Bathurst Describes a Circle; XII The Second Screen of Mary Stuart; XIII Colonel Leach-Fletcher Is at Home to Visitors; XIV Mr. Bathurst Takes a Book from the Bookcase; XV Mr. Daventry Gets His Feet Wet; XVI Mr. Bathurst Again Samples the Bookcase; XVII The Memoirs of Réné de St. Maure; XVIII The Room at Blanchard's Hotel; XIX Inspector Goodall Is Entertained; XX Mr. Bathurst Brushes Up His History; XXI Mr. Ferguson of New York; XXII Mr. Bathurst Baits the Hook; XXIII When the Cat's Away; XXIV The Secret of the Screens; XXV The Riddle of the Black Twenty-Two.

**Characters:**
- Peter Daventry: junior partner, solicitors "Merryweather, Linnell and Daventry" (Cornhill, London); Oxford man; brother Gerald Daventry (accountant, Wedderburn and Rathbone; M.C.C. member).
- David Linnell: senior partner, 58, Lancashire-born, Northerner.
- Plunkett: middle-aged clerk, 35 years' service.
- Collins: office messenger.
- Marriott: Peter's acquaintance at Law Courts.
- Gustave: waiter at the Violette restaurant (Oxford St.); proprietor Lironi.
- Laurence P. Stewart: American millionaire, widower, collector obsessed with Mary Queen of Scots relics; bought Assynton Lodge (near Wantage, Berkshire). Age 53 (birthday 22 July). Wife died ten years earlier.
- Charles Stewart: son, ~22, Stewart's son, called "Charles"/"Stewart."
- Colonel Leach-Fletcher: neighbour (house "Neuve Chapelle" on Rockinge road, ~4 miles); client of the firm; gives recommendation; drives Bentley (seventy-five mph); white moustache; dined at Assynton night of murder; says Stewart was worried about "treachery" and about son's conduct; Renan's *Vie de Jésus* on desk.
- Day, Forshaw and Palmers: auctioneers, Hanover Galleries, W.1. Partners: Mr. Day (tall), Ronald Forshaw (young, "Forshaw Junior").
- Mason: night-watchman murdered (skull bashed) at Hanover Galleries; Druce: older night-watchman (about 60, wizened, 6 years' service, daughter Poppy).
- Mrs. Turner: cleaner who raised alarm.
- Detective-Inspector Goodall: Scotland Yard, stout, clean-shaven, double-breasted blue serge; sidekick Waring; Doctor Archer (Hanover), Doctor Gunner (Assynton).
- Sergeant Clegg (Amos Clegg): local Assynton police; married 17 years; romantic; constable Potter.
- Morgan Llewellyn: secretary, early 30s, pince-nez, reddish-brown eyes; "M. L."; love-letter to Marjorie threatening.
- Butterworth (John): butler, 60+, ex-service of Sir Julian Kennedy (Washington); wife Mrs. Butterworth (housekeeper); daughter Alice Mortimer (née Butterworth). Murderer of Laurence Stewart.
- Marjorie Lennox: ward, "petite," retroussé nose, blue eyes; lied about being in library; accused Llewellyn; handkerchief with "M. L." found by Clegg.
- Anthony Bathurst: free-lance amateur sleuth; Uppingham and Oxford; excels at games; solved Considine Manor case; cool, grey eyes.
- Servants: Barton, Regan, Evans, Winter (maids); Mrs. Briggs (cook); Maidment (gardener); Patrick O'Connor (boot-boy, 18, bicycle); Michael O'Connor (foundry giant, black beard, six feet two).
- "Snoop" Mortimer / "Flash Alf": American crook; alias "Laurence Charles Stewart"; wife Alice (hay fever, black glasses).
- Blanchard: owner, Blanchard's Hotel, Clifford Street (Regent 9999); Atkins: porter; Rabjohns: chambermaid.
- Andrew Ferguson: of Crake and Ferguson, New York, Stewart's solicitors; arrives Berkshire on *Mauretania*.
- Rosemary Armitage: Charles's love, of "The Towers," seven miles away.
- Thibaut Girardier: Mary's Chief Armorer, made screens.

**Events in order:**
1. Peter, hungover, at Cornhill; Linnell shows letter from Stewart (Assynton Lodge, June 7th) commissioning purchase at Day, Forshaw & Palmers' sale, June 10th, Nos. 37 (Collar of Pearls), 38 (Antique Tapestry Fire-screen), 39 (Rosary of Amber Beads), "all having been indisputably the property of Mary, Queen of Scots." Commission from Colonel Leach-Fletcher's recommendation. Telegrams from Stewart: "Say! What the hell's biting you—when I say Buy—then Buy. Got that? Stewart."
2. Peter lunches at Violette; remarks "So's Mary, Queen of Scots" to Marriott after "Queen Anne's dead"; man at next table (with woman) knocks cruet to floor; woman's look; overheard "let's go to-morrow—not to-day."
3. Peter views items at Galleries; plain-clothes men; the screen has beadwork "JESUS CHRIST, GOD AND SAVIOUR"; corners: Scots Lion, fleur-de-lis, Leopards and Lilies of England.
4. Linnell suspects forgery; goes to Galleries June 10 morning; Lord Clavering's collection.
5. Night-watchman Mason murdered; Druce recounts woman asking route to Marble Arch; she sneezed walking away. Stolen: only the three items. Office door unlocked.
6. Peter telephones Linnell from Berkshire; Linnell calls Stewart's son's phone message; Peter goes to Leyton (Middlesex v Essex), finds Bathurst at Princes Club (squash).
7. Train 6:55 Paddington; Peter, Bathurst, Goodall travel together; Clegg meets them at Assynton.
8. Assynton: Stewart found dead in library at desk, skull smashed, pen in hand; note "Urgent in the morning! M. L."; revolver (5 chambers loaded, 1 fired) in LEFT dressing-gown pocket; key inside library door; French doors bolted.
9. Clegg finds "M. L." handkerchief in curtains. Butterworth says he heard Stewart and Miss Lennox voices ~10:10 pm.
10. Night 1:22 am: Bathurst hears prowler; Llewellyn returns.
11. Bathurst's morning investigation: Patrick O'Connor's bicycle marked with tar from road-repair; bicycle used night of murder.
12. Bathurst finds stones/mud in coal-scuttle; ink-bowl has grit; stone weapon from rockery pool (Peter wades in); fired-shot test; bullet found in *Memoirs of Réné de St. Maure* (848 pages) on top bookshelf.
13. Goodall finds Blanchard's Hotel call (11 minutes), registered as Mr. and Mrs. Laurence Charles Stewart from New York.
14. Colonel Leach-Fletcher interview: Renan's *Vie de Jésus* on desk.
15. Llewellyn's letter found in book: threatens; Miss Lennox.
16. Stewart's will: Marjorie £250,000 (trust till 40), Charles residue (till 45), marriage conditions; Llewellyn £300 annuity; Butterworth £500 p.a.
17. Bathurst reveals Miss Armitage; Charles wants to marry her; will's marriage clauses.
18. Blanchard's: chambermaid Rabjohns smells odour; Atkins: lady wore black glasses, said "my father."
19. Ricardo's supper; Bathurst explains Mortimer and screens.
20. Night raid at Assynton (via Colonel's Bentley, borrowed); arrest of Mortimer, Alice Mortimer, and Butterworth at French doors; Goodall: "James Mason... June 9th" and "Laurence P. Stewart... June 8th."
21. Revelation: screens' fish conceals cavity with **Twenty-Two Black Pearls of Lorraine**. "ICHTHUS" key: *Ιησοῦς Χριστός Θεός Σωτήρ*; "Timeo Danaos" (Virgil). Cardinal of Lorraine's gift.
22. Charles and Rosemary; Marjorie to get Charles's screen pearls as wedding gift.

Note: "M. L." on note was Bathurst's theory = "Merryweather, Linnell and Daventry."

## BOOK 2 of 2: "Dorothy" by Evelyn Raymond (1907)

**Chapters:** I How Dorothy Came; II A Postal Substitute; III At Johns Hopkins Hospital; IV Dorothy Gains in Wisdom; V Dorothy Entertains; VI Dorothy Goes Upon an Errand; VII An Office Seeker and a Client; VIII Tenants for No. 77; IX Strange Experiences; X The Flitting; XI Jim Barlow; XII Dorothy's Illness; XIII The Plumber and His Gossip; XIV The Biter Bit; XV The Flight in the Night; XVI A Good Samaritan; XVII A Sunday Drive; XVIII Conclusion.

**Characters:**
- Dorothy C. (Dorothy Chester): foundling left on Chesters' steps in spring, age ~1 on arrival, ~13 in story; brown curly hair, big brown eyes, yellow head; birthday April 1st; wrote note "Dorothy's Gardeen, her X mark."
- John Chester ("Johnnie," "father John"): postman, Brown Street No. 77, Baltimore; cheery; diagnosed locomotor ataxia; sent to Johns Hopkins; later to Skyrie.
- Martha Chester ("mother Martha"): tidy housewife, wife of John.
- Mrs. Betty Cecil Somerset-Calvert ("Miss Betty"): wealthy widow at Bellevieu; eagle-gate; Great Danes Peter and Ponce; coachman Ephraim; maid Dinah (Dinah's foreboding speech); cook; boy Methuselah Bonaparte Washington (Brown).
- Mabel Bruce: chum, plumber's daughter; father Mr. Bruce (plumber); mother Mrs. Bruce.
- Miss Georgia: vice-principal, teacher.
- Aunt Chloe: John's old aunt.
- Mr. Lathrop: postman friend; post-office.
- Postmaster (unnamed): kindly, refused Dorothy job.
- "Mr. Smith": crook lawyer, Howard Street; drugged milk; kidnapper.
- Mrs. Jane Jones and Bill Jones: tenants (Mrs. Jones is Mrs. Bruce's sister-in-law); Bill night watchman.
- Miranda Stott ("Mrs. Denim"): truck-farm woman, Tige the mastiff; son (Smith's accomplice, sick with measles).
- Jim Barlow: "long boy," shock-headed, orphan, barefoot, learns spelling; wins respect; Daniel St. John: old minister with gig, horse Nan; sings hymns.
- Kidder & Kidder: lawyers (elder Mr. Kidder ~80).
- Deerhurst-on-the-Heights: Mrs. Cecil's summer estate (Cornwall, NY); Skyrie: stone cottage where John and Martha go.

**Events in order:**
1. Spring; baby left on Chesters' steps in baby-wagon, note "thee child Is wun Yere an too Munths old... Burthday is aPrill Furst..." John says "Good-bye"; Mrs. Cecil questions him.
2. Dorothy spills milk, chokes in bonnet strings; wears white shoes later.
3. John diagnosed (ataxy locomotor); stops work; Dorothy substitutes as postal delivery; attacked by Danes at Bellevieu (dogs knock her down; hits head).
4. John collapses; Dorothy searches; runs to Johns Hopkins in storm; faints by "Christ the Healer" statue.
5. John in hospital; family to move to Skyrie (Hudson highlands, NY), old uncle's property.
6. Dorothy buys white shoes ($1.97), blistered; meets Mr. Smith on street.
7. Dorothy applies to postmaster for father's job; rejected.
8. Mr. Smith lures her to Howard Street office; drugged milk; carried into hack; wakes at truck-farm of Miranda Stott.
9. Dorothy catches measles; Jim tends her; secret "Smith" hidden there.
10. Newspaper advertises $500 reward; Jim and Dorothy escape; Dorothy's foot pierced by bramble; Daniel St. John rescues them.
11. Mrs. Cecil recognizes Dorothy, rescues her from pursuers; Jim goes with her.
12. Mrs. Cecil consults Kidder & Kidder; Smith is discharged clerk; Dorothy taken to Skyrie in the end. Final: Dorothy reunited with parents at Skyrie; Jim to work at Deerhurst under Mrs. Cecil.
